name: Amazon CloudSearch
tagline: AWS's original managed search service, closed to new customers since July 2024.
description: Amazon CloudSearch is a managed search service launched by AWS in 2012 and rebuilt on Apache Solr in 2014. It handles indexing, scaling and patching automatically and offers text, faceted, geo and structured queries over uploaded JSON or XML batches. AWS closed it to new customers on July 25, 2024; existing accounts can keep using it and still get security and availability fixes, but no new features. AWS points migrations to Amazon OpenSearch Service, which also brings vector search that CloudSearch never got.
statusNote: Closed to new customers on July 25, 2024; existing accounts keep running with fixes only and no new features. AWS recommends migrating to Amazon OpenSearch Service.

pricing.notes: Billed per search-instance hour by instance type, plus document batch uploads, IndexDocuments requests and data transfer. Only available to accounts already allowlisted.

scale.notes: Automatically adds partitions and replicas as data and traffic grow; optional Multi-AZ.

drivers: AWS SDKs (Java, Python, JavaScript, .NET, Go, Ruby, PHP)
strengths: Zero-ops: AWS manages scaling, patching and replicas
Faceting, highlighting, autocomplete and geo search
weaknesses: No longer accepting new customers; feature-frozen
Coarse relevance tuning compared with OpenSearch
Instance-hour pricing is expensive for small workloads
useCases: Simple faceted catalog search for legacy apps
